revenue_growth.note: 4.5% near-term — e-commerce growing 20%+ within total. Walmart Connect ads ~$4B and rising fast

revenue_growth_terminal.note: Y5 fade to 3.5%. E-commerce penetration matures by FY30; back toward GDP+ growth as ad business stabilizes

fcff_margin.note: FCF $12,700M / Revenue $680,985M = 1.87%. Classic retail: thin margin × huge volume. CapEx ~$23.7B (stores + automation)

fcff_margin_terminal.source: Ad business (Walmart Connect) + membership scale thesis
fcff_margin_terminal.note: 1.87% → 3.5% over 5yr — EXPANSION case. Walmart Connect ads (~80% margin) + Walmart+ subscriptions add high-margin layer on top of low-margin retail. Management guidance + analyst models support 3-4% blended FCF margin by FY30.

wacc.note: Sector WACC: Cost of equity 7.54% (Rf 4.18% + β 0.81 × ERP 4.23%) × 92.64% E-weight + after-tax cost of debt 3.97% × 7.36% D-weight. Low beta = consumer staple

net_debt.note: Total debt $45,800M - Cash $9,037M = $36,763M. WMT doesn't hoard cash; capital-intensive ops

shares_outstanding.note: Diluted weighted-average shares FY2025 ($M shares) — post 3:1 split Feb 2024

buyback_yield.note: Steady $5-10B/yr buyback program / ~$700B market cap = ~1% annual. WMT balances dividend + capex + buyback.

sbc_pct_revenue.note: SBC ~$0.9B / Revenue $681B = 0.1%. Lowest in dataset — retail workforce is hourly cash comp.

expected_output.tolerance_rationale: Hand DCF (g=4%, margin=1.87%, WACC=7.27%) → ~$31. Market trades ~$135 (huge premium for e-commerce growth optionality, Walmart Connect ad business, OneAtWMT, scale moat). Pure FCFF margin doesn't capture these. Range [$20, $90] captures conservative-textbook through optimistic bull DCF; market $138 well above any 5yr FCFF model.
